summary: Iter 92.8 backend regression — 13/13 GREEN. Verified the 3 new improvements end-to-end: (1) GET /api/community/me-stats returns user_id=user_f111693f1b00 with full shape (post_count/total_likes/comment_count/rank/total_leaders) and correctly returns rank=null when post_count=0 / int 1..total_leaders otherwise. (2) Feed-filter param /api/community/feed?feed=top|mine|liked|all all work: top is sorted by likes_count desc (verified pairwise), mine returns only test user's posts, liked returns only posts where liked_by_me=true, all (default) is newest-first. (3) Category filter regression (?category=win) still works. (4) PATCH /api/video-archive/{entry_id} rename round-trip persists custom_title via GET, empty/whitespace title → 400, unknown id → 404. (5) DELETE /api/video-archive/{entry_id} unknown id → 404 (destructive happy-path NOT exercised to preserve real history — owner-guard wiring proven via same Mongo filter as PATCH). (6) Regression: POST /api/community/posts creates+cleanup OK; GET /api/video-archive returns list newest-first with no _id leakage.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/community.py:51-60 — feed=top uses aggregation with $addFields likes_count + sort by [likes_count desc, created_at desc]. Correct pattern — MongoDB find() can't sort by $size, so aggregation is required. Tie-breaker on created_at is a nice touch.

routes/community.py:45-48 — feed=mine sets query.user_id and feed=liked sets query.likes (array-contains). Both correctly run through the standard find() path so author enrichment + liked_by_me + comment_count post-processing still applies uniformly. Good.

routes/community.py:93-143 — get_my_community_stats: single aggregation over the whole community_posts collection then in-memory rank lookup. Acceptable for current scale (<10k leaders). At ~50k+ posts consider $facet with $match on the user's row + a parallel count to avoid pulling the whole leaderboard into Python. Not urgent.

routes/video.py:544-557 — rename_video_entry: title is stripped+sliced to 160 chars before length check — empty after strip → 400, ok. Owner-guard uses the {entry_id, user_id} compound filter so unknown OR foreign-owned both produce 404 (correct — no info leak about existence of another user's entry).

routes/video.py:560-575 — delete_video_entry follows the same owner-guard pattern and best-effort cleans up mission_shares. Idempotent on the share-cleanup side (delete_many with no match returns 0 silently). Good.

Pydantic body model RenameVideoEntryIn (video.py:540-541) uses plain str — no max_length validator. Server-side .strip()[:160] handles it but for defence-in-depth Pydantic Field(max_length=200) would reject obvious abuse at parse time.
